question_en:
I am selecting a set of moderately difficult samples for manual review for a bacterial instance segmentation course. The attachment contains unlabeled micrographs left over from an old project; please trace them back to the corresponding official data release record. Use only the official descriptions for species, strain, and imaging type. Please answer the following questions:

In the test source images, if both DIC and Nile Red channels are provided for the same field of view, use only the DIC image. Look for images containing a continuous chain of at least five distinguishable cell bodies touching one another; do not use images where defocus, saturation, or cropping makes the connection relationships unclear. Then read the count of non-zero instances in the paired segmentation maps and group them by official species and imaging type. For each group, select the two visually compliant images with the fewest instances as the first batch of samples for manual review; if the instance counts are the same, sort by source filename. Please provide the filenames of the finally selected images by species and imaging type.

Answer format: First, provide the name and DOI of the official data release record in text, then use a table to list the finally selected image filenames by species and imaging type, with two images per group arranged in the order specified in the question.

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 8-1-D01-2

## Step 01 · Trace Public Data Records Using Micrographs

Action: Examine cell morphology and imaging texture to search for public bacterial instance segmentation datasets. Example query: DeepBacs mixed segmentation StarDist JE2 DIC dataset.

Evidence Observation: Official description matches DeepBacs – Mixed segmentation dataset and StarDist model v1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.5551009. The input source is training set training/source/JE2NileRed_oilp22_PMP_101220_001_1.tif, which cannot be treated as a test set candidate. Species and strain must be read from the official description, not diagnosed based on cell shape.

Evidence Links:
https://zenodo.org/records/5551009
https://github.com/HenriquesLab/DeepBacs/wiki/Segmentation

Result of this step: Located the official Zenodo release record and accompanying project documentation.

## Step 02 · Locate Data Attachments and Source Image/Mask Directories

Action: In the release record's attachment section, select DeepBacs_Data_Segmentation_StarDist_MIXED_dataset.zip, and view the compressed package directory and Notes description.

Evidence Observation: The saved compressed package has a measured size of 41,275,333 bytes and contains 387 directory/file members (the 41,203,645 bytes in the old catalogue do not match the actual file; during tracing, rely on the measured file size and MD5). The MD5 is 33f877551c38ead1e75884e63ef33094. Images are provided as TIFF members inside the compressed package; do not fabricate independent web addresses for them. When re-checking the release page on 2026-10-11, the first request returned 429; subsequently, the page was reopened from search results, confirming that the file list still shows the same attachments and MD5; attachment retrieval did not read content due to size limits.

Evidence Links:
https://zenodo.org/records/5551009
https://zenodo.org/records/5551009/files/DeepBacs_Data_Segmentation_StarDist_MIXED_dataset.zip?download=1

Result of this step: Associate each source image and paired segmentation map with the release page attachment name and the precise internal paths below.

## Step 03 · Exclude Training Images and Duplicate Imaging Channels

Action: Retain only ordinary .tif files located directly in test/source; when DIC and *_NR.tif are paired for the same field of view, exclude the duplicate Nile Red channel.

Evidence Observation: test/source originally had 35 images; 5 S. aureus DIC images each had one duplicate Nile Red channel, resulting in 30 independent candidates after deduplication. Training sets, test/target masks, directories, and description files are not counted as source image candidates.

Evidence Links:
https://zenodo.org/records/5551009
https://github.com/HenriquesLab/DeepBacs/wiki/Segmentation

Result of this step: 5 images of S. aureus, 15 of E. coli, and 10 of B. subtilis, totaling 30 images.

## Step 04 · Establish Groups from Official Descriptions

Action: Read the species, strain, imaging type, and pixel size for each source; do not use filename prefixes as the sole biological evidence.

Evidence Observation:

| Official Species | Strain | Adopted Imaging Type | Image Dimensions | Pixel Size/nm |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Staphylococcus aureus | JE2 | DIC widefield | 512×512 | 80 |
| Escherichia coli | MG1655 (CGSC #6300) | brightfield | 1024×1024 | 79 |
| Bacillus subtilis | SH130 | fluorescence | 1024×1024 | 65 |

Evidence Links:
https://zenodo.org/records/5551009
https://github.com/HenriquesLab/DeepBacs/wiki/Segmentation

Result of this step: Divided into three groups by official species + imaging type.

## Step 05 · Define Source Image Visual Inspection and Mask Counting Method

Action: First, look only at the source images to find at least five distinguishable cell bodies touching one another in a continuous chain; then read the instance annotations in the corresponding test/target files.

Evidence Observation: Groups where defocus, saturation, or cropping makes connection relationships unclear are not used as evidence. The count is the number of labels after removing 0 from unique(mask), not the number of non-zero pixels, not the number of connected components, and not max(mask). It is sufficient for the complete chain to be within the frame; the presence of other cells at the image edge does not automatically exclude the entire image.

Evidence Links:
https://zenodo.org/records/5551009
https://github.com/HenriquesLab/DeepBacs/wiki/Segmentation

Result of this step: Recorded visual conclusions and mask instance counts for all 30 images, then sorted only those that passed visual inspection.
